raw_text:
Here is a structured 12-week program for a 47-year-old female advanced lifter in early perimenopause, prioritizing bone-loading compound lifts with heat-management considerations. The plan emphasizes bone density and muscle maintenance, while respecting heat intolerance (no sauna, no fasted HIIT in heated environments, plan cooling after hard sessions).

Assumptions and notes
- Training frequency: 4 days/week (e.g., Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat) with optional mobility/rest days as needed.
- Primary goals: maintain/increase bone density, preserve/rebuild lean mass, improve strength, manage hot flashes through cooling strategies and appropriate intensity.
- Conditioning: light-to-moderate conditioning work included for recovery and heat adaptation.
- Nutrition: protein target 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight/day; adequate calcium/vitamin D; hydration strategy; post-workout nutrition within 60–90 minutes.
- Recovery: emphasis on sleep, cooling protocols, deload weeks, and tissue-quality work.
- Medical: GP clearance obtained; monitor for symptoms, adjust intensity if heat intolerance worsens.

Weekly structure overview
- Warm-up: 10–12 minutes general + 6–8 minutes mobility/floor work; 5 minutes light cardio or rowing at low to moderate intensity.
- Core lifts: major bone-loading compound movements (squat pattern, hinge pattern, push, pull, loaded carries) with emphasis on technique and progressive overload.
- Accessory work: strength and hypertrophy work to support bone density and joint health; include 1–2 unilateral/antagonist balance movements.
- Conditioning: light conditioning 1–2 days per week; avoid high-intensity in hot environments. Use cooling post-session.
- Deload/recovery: Week 4 and Week 9 incorporate planned deload or reduced-volume weeks.

Program by weeks (12 weeks)

Phase 1: Foundation and adaptation (Weeks 1–3)
Goals: re-establish technique, establish bone-loading stimulus with controlled loads, assess tolerance to heat, set baseline intensity.

Week 1 (Starting 2026-06-01)
- Session A: Lower-Body Strength (bone-loading emphasis)
  - Back Squat: 4 sets x 5 reps at 75% 1RM
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x6 at 60–65% 1RM
  - Leg Press (tempo focus): 3x8
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6 per leg
  - Glute-ham raise or Nordic hamstring: 3x6
  - Core: Plank 3x45s; Side plank 3x30s each side
- Session B: Upper-Body Push-Pull (bone-loading emphasis)
  - Barbell Bench Press: 4x5 at 75% 1RM
  - Bent-Over Barbell Row: 4x6
  - Overhead Press (strict): 3x5
  - Inverted Rows or Pull-Ups: 3x6
  - Dumbbell lateral raise: 3x12
  - Farmer’s Carry: 3x40s (heavy)
- Conditioning/Recovery: 20–25 minutes easy cardio (bike/elliptical) at low/moderate intensity; focus on cooling down (ice towels, air flow). Mobility: 10 minutes (hips, T-spine, shoulders)

Week 2
- Session A
  - Back Squat: 4x5 at 77–78% 1RM
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x6 at 62–65%
  - Leg Extension/Leg Curl superset: 3x8–10
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6 per leg
  - Hip Thrust: 3x8
  - Core: Pallof press 3x10 each side
- Session B
  - Bench Press: 4x5 at 77–78% 1RM
  - Barbell Row: 4x6
  - Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press: 3x6
  - Pull-Ups/Assisted: 3x6
  - Face Pulls: 3x12
  - Farmer’s Carry: 3x50s
- Conditioning/Recovery: 2 x 15–20 min steady-state cardio, ensure cooling post-session

Week 3
- Session A
  - Back Squat: 5x5 at 75–77% 1RM
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x5 at 65%
  - Glute Bridge with Barbell: 3x8
  - Walking Lunge: 3x8 per leg
  - core: Dead Bug progression 3x10
- Session B
  - Bench Press: 5x5 at 75–77% 1RM
  - Barbell Row: 4x6
  - Push-up with elevated feet: 3x8
  - Lat Pulldown: 3x8
  - Dumbbell Shrugs: 3x10
  - Farmer’s Carry: 3x45s
- Conditioning/Recovery: 15–20 minutes low-intensity cardio; post-workout cooling protocol

Phase 2: Progressive overload and bone stimulus refinement (Weeks 4–6)
Phase 2 introduces slight intensity deloads or volume adjustments to promote recovery, while continuing bone-loading stimuli with controlled progression.

Week 4 – Deload/Active Recovery
- Session A
  - Back Squat: 3x5 at 60% 1RM
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x6 at 55–60%
  - Leg Curl/Leg Extension: 2x8
  - Lunges (bodyweight or light DB): 2x8 per leg
  - Core: 2x30s Plank
- Session B
  - Bench Press: 3x5 at 60% 1RM
  - Barbell Row: 3x6
  - Overhead Press: 3x5 at 50–55%
  - Assisted Pull-Ups: 3x6
  - Face Pulls: 2x12
- Conditioning/Recovery: Optional mobility day; focus on breathing and cooling

Week 5
- Session A
  - Back Squat: 4x4 at 78–80% 1RM
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x5 at 65%
  - Hip Thrust: 3x6
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6 per leg
  - Core: 3x8 Ab wheel or dead bug
- Session B
  - Bench Press: 4x4 at 78–80%
  - Barbell Row: 4x6
  - Push Press: 3x5
  - Lat Pulldown: 3x8
  - Farmer’s Carry: 3x45–60s
- Conditioning/Recovery: 2 low-to-moderate cardio sessions; ensure cooling after sessions

Week 6
- Session A
  - Back Squat: 5x3 at 80–82% 1RM
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x5 at 65–70%
  - Glute Bridge with barbell: 3x8
  - Walking Lunges: 3x8 per leg
  - Core: Plank variations 3x45s
- Session B
  - Bench Press: 5x3 at 80–82%
  - Barbell Row: 4x6
  - Overhead Press: 3x5 at 60%
  - Pull-Ups/Chin-Ups: 3x6
  - Face Pulls: 3x12
- Conditioning/Recovery: 2 sessions of light cardio with hydration strategy

Phase 3: Peak bone-loading and stability focus (Weeks 7–9)
Goal: maximize bone-loading stimulus with solid technique while controlling heat exposure and raising neuromuscular efficiency.

Week 7
- Session A
  - Back Squat: 4x3 at 85% 1RM (week 7)
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x5 at 70%
  - Hip Thrust: 3x6
  - Step-Ups with dumbbells: 3x8 per leg
  - Core: Suitcase carry 2x45s per side
- Session B
  - Bench Press: 4x3 at 85%
  - Barbell Row: 4x5
  - Push Press: 3x5
  - Lat Pulldown: 3x8
  - Face Pulls: 3x12
- Conditioning/Recovery: 15–20 minutes light cardio; cooling protocol after

Week 8
- Session A
  - Back Squat: 4x4 at 82–84% 1RM
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x5 at 70%
  - Hip Thrust: 3x6
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6 per leg
- Session B
  - Bench Press: 4x4 at 82–84%
  - Barbell Row: 4x6
  - Overhead Press: 3x6
  - Pull-Ups/Chin-Ups: 3x6
  - Farmer’s Carry: 3x50s
- Conditioning/Recovery: Ensure post-session cooling and hydration

Week 9 – Deload or reduced volume (as needed)
- Session A
  - Back Squat: 3x5 at 60–65%
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x5 at 60–65%
  - Glute Bridge: 2x8
- Session B
  - Bench Press: 3x5 at 60–65%
  - Barbell Row: 3x6
  - Push-Ups: 3x8
  - Lat Pulldown: 3x8
- Conditioning/Recovery: Mobility and light cardio

Phase 4: Maximize strength maintenance and bone density (Weeks 10–12)
Goal: maintain high-quality bone-loading reps with solid technique, end on a constructive 12-week adaptation plan.

Week 10
- Session A
  - Back Squat: 4x4 at 80–83% 1RM
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x5 at 70%
  - Hip Thrust: 3x6
  - Walking Lunges: 3x8 per leg
- Session B
  - Bench Press: 4x4 at 80–83%
  - Barbell Row: 4x6
  - Push Press: 3x5
  - Lat Pulldown: 3x8
- Conditioning/Recovery: 15–20 min low-intensity cardio; post-workout cooling

Week 11
- Session A
  - Back Squat: 5x3 at 85% 1RM
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x5 at 72–75%
  - Hip Thrust: 3x6
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6 per leg
- Session B
  - Bench Press: 5x3 at 85%
  - Barbell Row: 4x6
  - Overhead Press: 3x5
  - Pull-Ups/Chin-Ups: 3x6
- Conditioning/Recovery: Mobility + cooling-focused recovery

Week 12 – Final testing and plan closing
- Test or recheck 1RM estimates safely with taper
  - Back Squat: work up to a top single at 90% target, or perform a controlled 3x3 at 85–88% if not testing maximum
  - Bench Press: top single at 90% or 3x3 at 85–88%
  - Optional: Deadlift or hip hinge variant testing if technique is solid
- Conditioning: light cardio 15–20 minutes, focus on cooling and recovery
- Recovery plan: plan next phase based on response, adjust loads and volume

General coaching notes
- Intensity progression: Use RPE or %1RM guidance for progression. If regaining technique or experiencing heat intolerance, back off 2–5% and/or reduce reps.
- Tempo: For bone loading and tendon health, use controlled tempos: e.g., descent 3–4 seconds, pause 0.5–1 second, ascent 1–2 seconds (especially for squats and presses).
- Rest periods: 2–4 minutes for main lifts; 1–2 minutes for accessory work.
- Heat management: 
  - Schedule sessions during cooler parts of the day or in climate-controlled gym.
  - Pre-cool with room temp hydration and, if acceptable, a cool shower or cold towel pre-session.
  - Post-session cooling: cold towel wrap, fans, isotonic drink cooled beverages, and 10–15 minutes of low-intensity recovery activity.
  - Avoid fasted high-intensity in heated environments; maintain hydration throughout sessions.
  - Wear breathable, moisture-wicking clothing; consider vapor barrier layers only if needed for longer sessions—prioritize body temperature regulation.
- Thermoregulation cues: If hot flashes are disruptive, lower intensity slightly and extend rest periods; incorporate breathing practice (box breathing or 4-4-4-4) during heat episodes to stay calm.
- Bone density considerations: Emphasize multi-joint, high-load lifts (squat, hinge, push, pull). Ensure progressive overload is applied gradually and technique is prioritized over load.
- Injury prevention: Warm-up specific mobility (hip flexors, T-spine thoracic extension, shoulders), include rotator cuff work (external rotations) 2x/week; ensure balance between anterior/posterior chain work.
- Nutrition and recovery:
  - Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day, distributed across meals.
  - Calcium: 1,000–1,200 mg/day; Vitamin D: 800–2000 IU/day depending on baseline levels.
  - Hydration: aim for 2–3 liters/day baseline; add electrolytes for longer sessions.
  - Post-workout: protein + carbohydrate within 60–90 minutes.
  - Sleep: target 7–9 hours; use wind-down routine and cool environment to reduce night sweats sleep disruption.
- Monitoring: Track symptoms (hot flashes, night sweats, energy), blood pressure if relevant, and RPE at sessions. Adjust plan based on tolerance and GP advice if symptoms worsen.

Progression philosophy
- Repetition-based progression: Look to add 2.5–5 kg to main lifts every 2–3 weeks if technique is solid and no adverse heat symptoms occur.
- If fatigue or heat symptoms worsen, shift to RIR-based progression (e.g., maintain reps but reduce load to keep RPE around 6–7/10) and emphasize volume management.
- Deload weeks are integrated (Weeks 4 and 9) to support recovery and heat tolerance adaptation.

Equipment suggestions
- Barbell and plates; adjustable incline/flat bench; dumbbells; pull-up bar or assisted machine; resistance bands; mobility tools (foam roller, lacrosse ball); trap bar optional for variance; conditioning options (bike, rower).

If you want, I can tailor the exact 12-week calendar with daily sessions, precise weights per exercise based on the client’s current 1RM estimates, and a nutrition template to meet her macros and bone-supportive micronutrients. Also I can add specific cooling protocols (ice towels, fans, positioning) linked to each hard session.
